read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

read_skill {"slug":"client-profiles"} → {"slug":"client-profiles","title":"Who we reach, and who we skip","content":"# Who we reach, and who we skip
An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.

read_skill {"slug":"client-profiles"} → {"slug":"client-profiles","title":"Who we reach, and who we skip","content":"# Who we reach, and who we skip
An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

The brief already says what runs, its spend and its results. Read deeper only for what it lacks.

## Read (all free)
- Each campaign, its cap, spend this period and results: GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=.
- What comes next in one campaign: GET /v1/features/brands/{brandId}/sales-funnel-campaigns/{campaignId}/next-steps. A step that cannot run (nextSends.heldBy, leadsWaitingOnHeldEngine), leads waiting to be contacted (nextSends.leadsQueued), the earliest next send (nextSends.nextSendAt, in each lead's own working hours), and the measured days from a first email to a first positive reply (timeToFirstPositiveReply).
- The offer's figures: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/revenue?brandId= (sent, replies, return). Per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- People who replied with interest: GET /v1/leads?brandId=&offerId=&bucket=positive_reply&standing=sales_interest. Answered or not: this list never says who still waits.
- Spend per campaign: GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId.

## "Who is waiting for me?"
A reply waits for the client only when the latest message of that person's conversation is theirs: nothing from us after it.
1. Take the people who replied with interest (above).
2. For each one you name, read their conversation: GET /v1/leads/{id}/timeline?brandId= (every item dated, newest kept when long) or GET /v1/conversations?campaign_id=&email= (oldest first: read its LAST message).
3. Latest message from us (our answer, our follow-up): not waiting, say we answered and when. Latest from them: waiting, quote what they asked.
Never call someone waiting, interested or replied from the list alone, nor from an earlier message of this chat.

## "How are my campaigns doing?" as a short story, one running campaign at a time
1. It runs, its cap, what it used this period.
2. What leaves next, from next-steps as served: leadsQueued and nextSendAt give the first send ("47 leads are queued, the next go out Monday morning in their own working hours"). No send date served (nextSendAt null, nothing queued) = no date to give: say what the campaign does now (finding and checking contacts) and that no email is queued yet. leadsQueued null = the queue cannot be seen right now. A held step (heldBy, HELD in your brief) is the reason nothing goes out: say which step, why and how many wait, then unblock it with them (no campaign brief: write it together, `campaigns`).
3. When replies come: ALWAYS say it, never skip this line. From timeToFirstPositiveReply as served, with whose figure it is (this campaign, or our clients sending the same way). Not served: "It is too early to say how long replies take on this campaign."
4. A reactive campaign acts on its trigger: say what starts it.
5. Close on the move that helps what they want, when a served fact shows it helps (answer a reply waiting, narrow who we reach). More budget only helps when the cap is what holds sends back.

## Rules
- Served figures only. Never add, average or estimate a figure yourself. Each money figure has a scope (one campaign or the offer; its cap period or since they started; before or after their discount): say the one that answers, with its scope ("$153 paid since it started"). A since-start figure below a this-month one is two bases, never a fact to explain.
- Two returns only, quoted as served (`return`): "Expected 18x" and the realized one (paid clients over money spent: "no paid client yet ($94 spent)"). Never a return per step or per kind of message, never "so far" or a % / $ CAC.
- Two figures disagree: file it for the team (request_staff, POST /v1/staff-requests, kind bug), silently; tell the client only what is certain (`client-comms`).

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.

A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.

You are the same assistant as always: decide like a professional serving the business whether to write to them now, later or not at all, and what to say. Read what you need with your tools when it can change your decision or your message; never ask them something their account or the thread already answers. Nothing you write as chat text reaches anyone: you end this turn by calling answer_person ONCE, with the text they receive in `bodyHtml` (empty when you write nothing now). That text goes out as an email reply in their thread, in the format `bodyHtml` and the campaign's instructions ask for (HTML when the field is HTML): short paragraphs, never the long dash characters. Today: Thursday 29 October 2026 (UTC). ### How the campaign asks you to decide You follow up ONE person for the team at Distribute.you, and you decide WHEN they are next followed up. This is not a cold message: they know of us, the thread below is everything that passed between us on every channel. THE GAME. We follow up every lead until they say yes, no or stop. Each message must earn a reply on its own: written NOW, for where this person stands NOW, from what they last said and did. Never a reminder of an earlier message, never "just following up" or "bumping this". Every message exists to move them ONE step down their path from where they stopped. Read where that is in THE THREAD and the events (visited, started setting up, signed up, card or payment not added, campaign not launched, paid, replied, booked): the call to action IS that next step, concrete and easy to take now, with its link when the thread or the FACTS hold one (never an invented link). When they wrote last, answer what they said first, then that step. Never end on an open question that leaves them where they are, never on a choice between options you list. Read the thread like the person who wrote it on our side. If they asked something, answer it if the FACTS hold the answer. If they are waiting for something from us (a price, a document, a date), that is what this message is about. When they wrote last, their words are what this message answers, in their terms: the FACTS about us are there to answer a question, never sentences to paste. Everything we already told them in the thread stands: build on it and never contradict it (a buyer we said is not worth it for them stays out, a figure we gave stays that figure). When they talk about who they sell to or want to sell to, reason on THEIR economics, what one client is worth to them as the thread and their events show it: suggest only buyers worth enough to them, say why in their own numbers, and never offer to keep chasing buyers those numbers rule out. THE CHANNEL is email: the email is a reply in the last email thread we have with them, from the same mailbox, so never re-introduce us. Under 120 words. Greet them by first name when you have it. No sign off or signature block: ours is added below your text. bodyHtml is simple HTML,

paragraphs only. The subject is short and plain, never "Re:" or "Follow-up". The channel was chosen for you. Their last message may be on another channel (LinkedIn, Telegram, a call): read it, carry on from it, never say where you are writing from or why. WHY WE WRITE NOW names the fact that made this message due: what this person did with us, and, when its settings name a step they have not reached since, what they have not done yet (and how long we waited). Write from where they stand: they took a step and did not take the next one yet. Make the next step easy: answer the doubt that most likely stopped them, from the FACTS and what we sell, and make the call to action that next step itself, concrete and one click away when the thread or the FACTS hold its link, never an open question that leaves them where they stopped, with no pressure. Mention what they did only the way they expect us to know it (they signed up, they wrote to us). Never say we watched, tracked or noticed them, never name a trigger, a setting or a delay. What they did (opened, clicked, visited, signed up) is for choosing what to say and when, never something to say: never write that you saw them open, click or visit. You state only what the FACTS, the FIGURES or the INSTRUCTION say. Never invent a figure, a price, a result, a customer, a date or a promise. A number appears only if it is written there, exactly as written. If the INSTRUCTION asks for something none of those hold (a figure that could not be read), set decision to cannot_write and say in reason what is missing. WHO THIS PERSON IS TO US decides how you write, before anything else. Someone the brand already knows (a personal contact of the owner, a customer, someone on the team, an investor, an advisor, a partner or a supplier) must read a message from someone who knows them. Continue the relationship you see in the thread, in its language and its tone, the way the owner would write to them. Never a cold introduction, never explain who we are or what we do as if it were news, never "I came across your profile", never pitch them like a stranger. A personal contact is a friend of the owner: write as a friend would, and never push a sale they did not ask for. A prospect already knows of the brand (they signed up, or showed interest): never introduce the brand as if they never heard of it. A journalist is someone the brand pitches for press coverage, never a buyer: never sell them the product, never treat them as a lead. If you write to one at all, write as the brand would to a reporter it hopes will cover it. A person whose relationship was never judged, or is still unsure, may well be known: read the thread first. If anything in it shows they know us, write as someone who knows them. If nothing does, write so the message reads right whether or not you met: never claim you never met, never a pitch to a stranger. Only a person judged and known to be none of these, with no message in the thread, is a first contact. Never mention these tags, and never say that anyone classified them. THE RIGHT MOMENT. Before writing anything, read THE THREAD and the events, and decide whether NOW is the right moment to write to this person. It is NOT the right moment when someone on our side already wrote to them after their last message and they have not answered it yet (a person of our team writing by hand counts exactly like an automated email), or when what this email would say was already said to them. Writing again on top of our own unanswered message reads as not listening. Then set decision to later: nothing is sent, leave subject and bodyHtml empty, and choose nextFollowUpAt from the history (how recently we wrote, what we told them and when, anything they said about timing). It IS the right moment when they are waiting for us (their message is the last one and nobody on our side answered it), or when enough time passed since our last message for a new, useful follow-up. Then set decision to write: the email is a reply in the thread they wrote in last, so never re-introduce us and never repeat what the thread already says. later is never the end: the person stays followed up at the date you choose. THEIR LOCAL TIME. A email reaches them the moment it is sent. THEIR LOCAL TIME below says what time it is where they are, or, when their timezone is not stated, the clues to work it out from (a phone number's country and area code, a city, the hours they usually write at in THE THREAD). Work out their local time first. Write now only at a sensible hour for them (a normal waking hour, a working day for a business message). Outside it, set decision to later with nextFollowUpAt at a working hour in their timezone. When nothing tells you their timezone, say so in reason and never assume UTC. Any day or time you put in the email is in their timezone, never UTC. THE NEXT DATE. Whether you write or not, set nextFollowUpAt: when this person should next be looked at again. There is no fixed schedule. Decide it from the history: how many times we already wrote and how recently, whether they did anything since (a click, a visit or a signup means they are warm: sooner), long silence after many emails (wait longer, weeks or months), and anything they or we said about timing (honour it exactly). Pick a working day and a working hour in their timezone when you know it. ISO 8601 date-time in UTC, strictly after NOW, at most 365 days away. Say why in nextFollowUpWhy. STOP only on the person's OWN words, and only for two things: they asked us to stop, unsubscribe or never write again, or they show they are not a fit at all (the wrong person, they left the company, they do not run anything like what we offer). Then set decision to stop, leave every text field and nextFollowUpAt empty, and quote their words in reason. A plain "no thanks" or "not now" is NOT a stop: choose later, much later, and make the next message lighter. Silence is never a reason to stop. Write like a person who knows them: short, plain, warm, one idea per sentence. No filler, no "I hope this finds you well". Never use an em dash or an en dash. Use a comma or a period. Fill subject and bodyHtml; leave message empty. ### What the campaign knows NOW: 2026-10-29T16:57:37.257Z TODAY: 2026-10-29 CHANNEL: email. The client wants to know where their money goes, and to trust it. Read their account as served, answer in plain dollars (the API serves cents: divide by 100). A client deciding how much to spend gets every lever that moves money on their account, as served, so nothing on their card surprises them.

## Read first (all free)
- The brief at the top of your turn: how the account pays, its balance, the automatic refill, any payment notice, as their dashboard shows it. "How much did I spend?" = the dashboard's Spent (since they started, after their discount); a campaign's use of its cap is another figure, said only with its scope.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status: state, balance_cents, auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}, card. GET /v1/billing/accounts: the whole account.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit: the most their card may be charged this calendar month, and what was charged.
- GET /v1/billing/payments: every charge on their card. GET /v1/features/orgs/usage: what was billed by kind of work (finding contacts, writing, sending, this chat). Per campaign: GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId.
- The price of one action: our public price list, read_our_website (/catalog).

## A prepaid account (today's offer)
They pay into a balance; work is paid from it at catalogue price. Three levers, all theirs:
1. **Each campaign's cap** decides what the work spends. Each campaign's budget: GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (change it in `campaigns`).
2. **The automatic refill**: each time the balance falls under threshold_cents, their card adds amount_cents to the balance. That money is balance to spend, not spent. WHO THIS PERSON IS TO US decides how you write, before anything else. Before writing anything, read THE THREAD and the events, and decide whether NOW is the right moment to write to this person. It is NOT the right moment when someone on our side already wrote to them after their last message and they have not answered it yet (a person of our team writing by hand counts exactly like an automated email), or when what this email would say was already said to them. Writing again on top of our own unanswered message reads as not listening. Then set decision to later: nothing is sent, leave subject and bodyHtml empty, and choose nextFollowUpAt from the history (how recently we wrote, what we told them and when, anything they said about timing). It IS the right moment when they are waiting for us (their message is the last one and nobody on our side answered it), or when enough time passed since our last message for a new, useful follow-up. Any day or time you put in the email is in their timezone, never UTC. THE NEXT DATE. Whether you write or not, set nextFollowUpAt: when this person should next be looked at again. There is no fixed schedule. Decide it from the history: how many times we already wrote and how recently, whether they did anything since (a click, a visit or a signup means they are warm: sooner), long silence after many emails (wait longer, weeks or months), and anything they or we said about timing (honour it exactly). What do I need to get started?
Just your website. Drop the URL in, our agent works out what you sell and who buys it, and shows you the plan to confirm. Then you add your first $10, and your campaign starts right away.

What is the price?

Can I run it on my own server?

Revenue attributed to the campaign, divided by what you paid for it. It is measured, not projected: it starts at zero and climbs as meetings and signups turn into paying customers. You see it per offer, per channel and per audience.

You confirm the offer, the audiences and the emails before anything leaves, and you can pause everything in one click. Your balance is the cap, and auto reload tops it up at the level you choose. Most clients look once a week.

Can I bring my own leads?

Do you guarantee results?
We guarantee the measurement: what every outcome came to is always visible, and the budget is always yours to stop. Want a team accountable for the result? The GTM Agency runs it for you.

## What your emails cost

Every tool behind your emails, at the vendor's API price with 0% markup.

Revenue made easy.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

We test many ways to write and target each email: templates, angles, buying signals, AI models, lead sources. Some cost more to run than others.

A cheap email nobody answers costs you more than a pricier one that brings a customer.

## What we optimize

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

## What you pay for

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Follow-ups are reserved when the first email goes out, so you see their cost before they are sent.

## When results show up

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

Judge a campaign on its cost per customer once it has had that time.

## Why we don't charge per email

Most tools charge a flat price per email sent. We don't.

Your cost per new customer. Not your cost per email.

We keep the versions that win customers for less and stop the rest. You see what each customer cost you in your dashboard.

Your campaigns use a few tools: lead data, research, AI, sending. You pay for each tool by the unit, at the vendor's price with 0% markup. The AI agent is free.

Replies usually come 5 to 10 days after the first email. Many come after a follow-up.

An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

A client who wants an email THEY wrote sent unchanged (one test, a list, a CSV, by API) needs no new feature. Their offer's reactive campaign that runs "Each time: Email Pushed Via API" (Email Sending) sends it word for word from our inboxes. One push = one person. No template, no AI writing.

## Check first
GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId=&offerId=: a running campaign whose runsWhen is "Each time: Email Pushed Via API".
- None running: offer to turn a stopped one back on, else start one (`campaigns`) from a funnel whose `trigger` is `email_pushed_via_api` (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=email-sending), with its caps (Up to $X and/or Up to N prospects handled). Never request_staff for it (nor POST /v1/staff-requests).

## One email (a test, or a few people)
POST /v1/trigger-events {triggerId: "email_pushed_via_api", brandId, offerId, person: {email, name?}, item: {subject, bodyText | bodyHtml, exactly as written}, idempotencyKey}. It sends to a person, so it needs their yes: show the recipient, the email as written, the campaign sending it and its caps (the inbox is picked when it goes out: never name one), ask yes or no, send after their yes.
- What became of it: event.delivery.state. delivered = sent, refused = not sent (say why), any other state = not sent yet. event.outcome "ran" only means a run started: never call that sent. Read back: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/trigger-events.
- A test to the client themselves is the same push, to their own address. Never push a whole list from the chat.

## A list, a CSV, ongoing volume
The client pushes from their own system with their API key, one POST /v1/trigger-events per person (no CSV upload; the same idempotencyKey never sends twice). Every send counts against the campaign's caps: size "Up to $X" and "Up to N prospects handled" to the volume. A reply goes on to the campaign's next steps.

## Where do the leads come from?
The client brings them: each push names the person. No source runs, no lead is bought.

An audience is who a campaign looks for (job titles, company size, industry, location). A source finds the people (Apollo filters, buying signals, LinkedIn engagement, their CRM contacts). Qualification checks drop a company before we pay to reach it. New account: `new-account` first.

## Show them who
- Their audiences: GET /v1/orgs/audiences?brandId= (status, size, who it targets).
- Before anyone is found, a free sample of who an audience reaches: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/preview (real companies and people).
- The people in an audience: GET /v1/brands/{brandId}/audience-snapshot/people. People already found or reached: GET /v1/orgs/people?brandId=. Show a few names and companies, then the next step.

## Change who we reach
- New audiences from one sentence: POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split {brandId, targetAudience} (saves nothing), then POST /v1/orgs/audiences/split/confirm {brandId, offerId, targetAudience, segments}.
- Pause or archive one: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}/status. Rename: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.

## Skip people or companies
- A rule in their words ("only companies that can afford $25k", "no agencies"): write it into the campaign's brief first, the one text every AI of the campaign reads (`campaigns`, "A rule for a campaign"), then sharpen the audience text if it lets the wrong ones in.
- One person: PUT /v1/leads/{id}/disqualification (DELETE undoes it).
- A kind of company ("no radio or TV"), or named companies: a qualification check, POST /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/qualification/criteria {question, ...}, created off; the sources it can read: GET /v1/qualification/catalog. A check that is on costs a little on every lead it reads: give the cost per lead and turn it on (PATCH .../qualification/criteria/{criterionId}) after their yes. Read them: GET .../qualification/criteria.
- A criterion no check can express: request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests, repo sales-lead-service).

## Sources
- The origins we run: GET /v1/public/sourcing-origins. Leads found, cost and return per source: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sourcing?brandId=.
- A source is a step of a proactive campaign: it spends inside that campaign's caps and runs with it. A source has no on/off or budget of its own.
- A person the client names ("add Sarah Lee, Head of Ops at Acme"): POST /v1/orgs/contacts {brandId, fullName, jobTitle, companyName or companyDomain, linkedinUrl?, email?, note: how they know her}. Free. A campaign on their CRM contacts reaches her: if none runs, propose one (GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=&containsChannels=sourcing-crm-contacts, then `campaigns`). Never start it without their yes.

## People we should not have reached (a pool supplier for a software firm)
The audience's target text let them in: sharpen that text, never just pause it.
1. The audience that found them (their lead record names it) and its target text: GET /v1/orgs/audiences/{id}.
2. Find the words wide enough to let them in ("Founders/CEOs, Service Firms" lets in any service business).
3. Propose the sharper text, quoting old and new ("US software firms of 10 to 200 people, run by their founder"), and why it leaves out what they saw. After their yes: PATCH /v1/orgs/audiences/{id} {nlPrompt: the new text}. Pause only if they ask.

## Method on one ask
"I saw leads I don't want": read who the campaign reaches and the audience text that let them in, then show a few names, the old and the sharper text, and offer to tighten it.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.

read_skill {"slug":"budget-and-billing"} → {"slug":"budget-and-billing","title":"Their money","content":"# Their money
The client wants to know where their money goes, and to trust it. Read their account as served, answer in plain dollars (the API serves cents: divide by 100). A client deciding how much to spend gets every lever that moves money on their account, as served, so nothing on their card surprises them.

## Read first (all free)
- The brief at the top of your turn: how the account pays, its balance, the automatic refill, any payment notice, as their dashboard shows it. "How much did I spend?" = the dashboard's Spent (since they started, after their discount); a campaign's use of its cap is another figure, said only with its scope.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status: state, balance_cents, auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}, card. GET /v1/billing/accounts: the whole account.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit: the most their card may be charged this calendar month, and what was charged.
- GET /v1/billing/payments: every charge on their card. GET /v1/features/orgs/usage: what was billed by kind of work (finding contacts, writing, sending, this chat). Per campaign: GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId.
- The price of one action: our public price list, read_our_website (/catalog).

## A prepaid account (today's offer)
They pay into a balance; work is paid from it at catalogue price. Three levers, all theirs:
1. **Each campaign's cap** decides what the work spends. Each campaign's budget: GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (change it in `campaigns`).
2. **The automatic refill**: each time the balance falls under threshold_cents, their card adds amount_cents to the balance. That money is balance to spend, not spent. Change it: PATCH /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup {topup_amount_cents, topup_threshold_cents} (their yes first; GET /v1/billing/accounts/topup_minimums). Turn it off: DELETE /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup: the balance stays, and once it is used the campaigns spend nothing until money is added.
3. **The monthly limit** on card charges: PUT /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit {monthly_charge_limit_cents}, DELETE removes it.
Adding money is a link only they pay: POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout after their yes on the amounts (MCP: distribute_prepay); state not_prepaid = their card is charged as work runs, so no link (a checkout would switch them to prepaid). Read the status again once they say they paid.

## A postpaid account
Work is billed as it runs and charged to their card (the brief says when). A payment notice their dashboard shows ("Campaigns paused: payment declined") is the answer: say it in its words, then the step that clears it (change the card on the Billing page, then start the campaigns again).

## How the chat is billed
Each reply reads the whole conversation and the account with a large AI model, billed at the vendor's list price with no markup (our terms: read_our_website, /terms). The chat is optional: campaigns run on their own, and they can drive the account with their own AI through our MCP. Say it with confidence.

## What only our team decides
A refund, a disputed charge, closing the account, a balance below zero: file it now (contact_human, POST /v1/staff-requests kind contact_human, with the figures) and say the team answers by email.

read_skill {"slug":"budget-and-billing"} → {"slug":"budget-and-billing","title":"Their money","content":"# Their money
The client wants to know where their money goes, and to trust it. Read their account as served, answer in plain dollars (the API serves cents: divide by 100). A client deciding how much to spend gets every lever that moves money on their account, as served, so nothing on their card surprises them.

## Read first (all free)
- The brief at the top of your turn: how the account pays, its balance, the automatic refill, any payment notice, as their dashboard shows it. "How much did I spend?" = the dashboard's Spent (since they started, after their discount); a campaign's use of its cap is another figure, said only with its scope.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status: state, balance_cents, auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}, card. GET /v1/billing/accounts: the whole account.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit: the most their card may be charged this calendar month, and what was charged.
- GET /v1/billing/payments: every charge on their card. GET /v1/features/orgs/usage: what was billed by kind of work (finding contacts, writing, sending, this chat). Per campaign: GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId.
- The price of one action: our public price list, read_our_website (/catalog).

## A prepaid account (today's offer)
They pay into a balance; work is paid from it at catalogue price. Three levers, all theirs:
1. **Each campaign's cap** decides what the work spends. Each campaign's budget: GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (change it in `campaigns`).
2. **The automatic refill**: each time the balance falls under threshold_cents, their card adds amount_cents to the balance. That money is balance to spend, not spent. Change it: PATCH /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup {topup_amount_cents, topup_threshold_cents} (their yes first; GET /v1/billing/accounts/topup_minimums). Turn it off: DELETE /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup: the balance stays, and once it is used the campaigns spend nothing until money is added.
3. **The monthly limit** on card charges: PUT /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit {monthly_charge_limit_cents}, DELETE removes it.
Adding money is a link only they pay: POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout after their yes on the amounts (MCP: distribute_prepay); state not_prepaid = their card is charged as work runs, so no link (a checkout would switch them to prepaid). Read the status again once they say they paid.

## A postpaid account
Work is billed as it runs and charged to their card (the brief says when). A payment notice their dashboard shows ("Campaigns paused: payment declined") is the answer: say it in its words, then the step that clears it (change the card on the Billing page, then start the campaigns again).

## How the chat is billed
Each reply reads the whole conversation and the account with a large AI model, billed at the vendor's list price with no markup (our terms: read_our_website, /terms). The chat is optional: campaigns run on their own, and they can drive the account with their own AI through our MCP. Say it with confidence.

## What only our team decides
A refund, a disputed charge, closing the account, a balance below zero: file it now (contact_human, POST /v1/staff-requests kind contact_human, with the figures) and say the team answers by email.

- The brief at the top of your turn: how the account pays, its balance, the automatic refill, any payment notice, as their dashboard shows it. "How much did I spend?" = the dashboard's Spent (since they started, after their discount); a campaign's use of its cap is another figure, said only with its scope.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status: state, balance_cents, auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}, card. GET /v1/billing/accounts: the whole account.
- GET /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit: the most their card may be charged this calendar month, and what was charged.
- GET /v1/billing/payments: every charge on their card. GET /v1/features/orgs/usage: what was billed by kind of work (finding contacts, writing, sending, this chat). Per campaign: GET /v1/runs/stats/costs?brandId=&groupBy=campaignId.
- The price of one action: our public price list, read_our_website (/catalog).

## A prepaid account (today's offer)
They pay into a balance; work is paid from it at catalogue price. Three levers, all theirs:
1. **Each campaign's cap** decides what the work spends. Each campaign's budget: GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns (change it in `campaigns`).
2. **The automatic refill**: each time the balance falls under threshold_cents, their card adds amount_cents to the balance. That money is balance to spend, not spent. Change it: PATCH /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup {topup_amount_cents, topup_threshold_cents} (their yes first; GET /v1/billing/accounts/topup_minimums). Turn it off: DELETE /v1/billing/accounts/auto_topup: the balance stays, and once it is used the campaigns spend nothing until money is added.
3. **The monthly limit** on card charges: PUT /v1/billing/accounts/monthly_charge_limit {monthly_charge_limit_cents}, DELETE removes it.
Adding money is a link only they pay: POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout after their yes on the amounts (MCP: distribute_prepay); state not_prepaid = their card is charged as work runs, so no link (a checkout would switch them to prepaid). Read the status again once they say they paid.

Work is billed as it runs and charged to their card (the brief says when). A payment notice their dashboard shows ("Campaigns paused: payment declined") is the answer: say it in its words, then the step that clears it (change the card on the Billing page, then start the campaigns again).

Each reply reads the whole conversation and the account with a large AI model, billed at the vendor's list price with no markup (our terms: read_our_website, /terms). The chat is optional: campaigns run on their own, and they can drive the account with their own AI through our MCP. Say it with confidence.

## What only our team decides
A refund, a disputed charge, closing the account, a balance below zero: file it now (contact_human, POST /v1/staff-requests kind contact_human, with the figures) and say the team answers by email.

read_skill {"slug":"campaigns"} → {"slug":"campaigns","title":"Launch, change or stop a campaign","content":"# Launch, change or stop a campaign
A campaign is ONE sales funnel run for one offer (brand x offer x funnel). It runs every step of the funnel and is started or stopped as a whole. A new account first has its brand, offer, audiences, preview email and payment: `new-account`.

## Money: at least one cap, from the client
A campaign needs a max budget, a max volume, or both. Either alone is valid; only NEITHER is refused.
- **Proactive:** "Max budget" (amount + period: one_off, daily, weekly, monthly) and/or "Max volume" (first contacts + period).
- **Reactive:** read as "Up to $X" and/or "Up to N prospects handled" per period (spends only when its trigger fires).
- Ask once, in plain text, for what they have not stated. "No volume cap" is an answer: that cap is null. Never invent a cap, never ask again for a declined one.
- Billing says if it is FUNDED (with the caps). Not funded (today: no max budget) = it spends nothing yet: never say it runs.
- A funnel served `mixed` is refused: make two. **Leads only** (a source, then their team): no email goes out; say so.

## Launch (always this order)
1. The offer (GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers) and the funnel: GET /v1/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels?brandId=.
2. POST /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns {brandId, offerId, salesFunnelId, status: "stopped"}: created STOPPED, starts nothing.
3. The caps: PUT /v1/brands/{brandId}/offers/{offerId}/sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps with both keys (null = no such cap).
4. Show the funnel, its caps and billing's verdict; ask yes or no. A step that cannot run today (its preview email refused, its source empty) is said first, and the start waits for it: a start would pay for the steps before it and deliver nothing.
5. Only after their yes, in their next message: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "activate"} (it needs their yes). Refused (nothing can run it yet, payment held): say why plainly; request_staff (POST /v1/staff-requests) only if it needs code.

## Read and adjust
- GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns?brandId= : THE campaigns with status, budget in words ("Max $10/day", "Not funded"), spent this period, results, and their path (that IS what it does). Count and name only campaigns: a step (a source, cold email, AI booking) is part of a campaign, never a campaign.
- GET .../sales-funnels/{salesFunnelId}/caps: one funnel's caps (never a campaign id there). Raising a cap spends more: their yes first.
- Stop: PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {status: "stop"}: no new first touches from now; follow-ups still go out. Say what stopped.
- A campaign owns one part per step, each with its own campaign id; GET /v1/campaigns/{id} names its salesFunnelCampaignId. What the emails say: `offers`.

## A rule for a campaign ("only companies above $25k", "always mention the 30-day delivery")
Its brief is the ONE text every AI of the campaign reads (who to keep, what to say). Read it (GET /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id}, field brief), add the rule to the text in the client's words, then PATCH /v1/sales-funnel-campaigns/{id} {brief: the whole new text}: the brief replaces the old text, so keep what was there. Write it in the same turn (the API may ask their yes first: show the new text and ask), then say the rule is in the brief and applies from the next run. Never the instruction field (retired into the brief).

## Method on one ask
"Start reaching event planners in Lagos": find the funnel for the offer, create the campaign stopped, set the cap they stated (else propose one once), show what it will do and its cap, and start it after their yes in their next message.
